DAWBA is a manualized and semi-structured diagnostic interview method used in child and adolescent psychiatry in Denmark [^src1] [^src2]. It is specifically utilized for the systematic and cross-sectional assessment of core ADHD symptoms, differential diagnoses, and comorbid conditions in children and adolescents [^src1] [^src2]. 

Within the Danish national quality monitoring framework for ADHD diagnostics, DAWBA is recognized as one of three approved interview methods—alongside Kiddie-SADS and PSE-SCAN—for fulfilling [[indicator-2b|indicator 2b]] (also referred to in annual reports as [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]]) [^src1] [^src2]. This clinical quality indicator measures the proportion of diagnostic assessment processes for patients aged 6 to 17 where a structured interview or clinical environmental observation is completed within 120 days of the assessment's initiation [^src1]. The use of standardized tools like DAWBA is central to national efforts, tracked via the ADHD-DATABASEN, to ensure diagnostic certainty, geographic equality, and adherence to clinical guidelines across regions and treatment facilities [^src1] [^src2].
